subject: Access snapshot + SAML assertion traces for SOC2/SIG review
messages:
From: Rachel Peters <rachel.peters@healthbridge.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Evidence request: access snapshot + SAML assertion traces for SOC 2 review

Hi Ava,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call yesterday. As part of our SOC 2 and SIG assessment we need a short evidence package focused on access control and identity flows. Can you provide the following: 

- A point-in-time access snapshot listing active user accounts, service accounts, roles and last login timestamps (CSV preferred)
- SAML assertion logs for the last 30 days (including both successful and failed assertions) — redacted where appropriate
- SCIM provisioning events/delta export for the last 60 days (or a compressed archive of the export)
- Current RBAC role matrix (mapping of roles to permissions and examples of least-privilege assignments)

Our assessor would like to see the above items by COB PT Friday (2026-10-08). If any of these are not available in the requested format, let us know the earliest ETA and a short description of how the data is produced.

Also confirm whether any of the artifacts contain PII so we can plan redaction.

Appreciate it — let me know if you want to quick sync.

Thanks,
Rachel Peters
Security Program Manager
HealthBridge

Attachment: request_scoping_sheet.xlsx (stub)

From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Rachel Peters <rachel.peters@healthbridge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-10-04T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: access snapshot + SAML assertion traces for SOC 2 review

Hi Rachel —

Thanks for the clear list. We'll get this pulled together. Quick notes:

- I'm looping in Marissa from our Security & Compliance team to own the artifact collection and ensure redaction where needed. Ben (cc) is our account lead and will coordinate timing if we need to extend the ETA.
- We can produce an access snapshot CSV and a role matrix workbook. SAML assertion logs are available as raw event logs; we'll include a small sample text export plus guidance on how to interpret the fields.
- SCIM deltas can be provided as an export; we'll indicate the exact attribute mapping so you can reconcile to your template.

Can you confirm whether the assessor needs the failed and successful assertion samples separated, and whether we should include any raw IP addresses (we typically redact IPs unless requested otherwise)?

Targeting an initial bundle by end of day Thursday (2026-10-07). If that timeline doesn't work, tell us and we'll prioritize differently.

Thanks —
Ava
Ava Chen
Senior Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2026-10-05T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: access snapshot + SAML assertion traces for SOC 2 review

Hi Rachel / Ava,

Thanks — this is straightforward. Below is the planned deliverable set and a short explanation of formats so your assessor can parse them quickly: 

1) access_snapshot_20261004.csv (attached) — a point-in-time export from our identity catalog listing: subject_id, principal_type (user/service), email, primary_role, last_successful_login_utc, account_status. We have excluded hashed MFA tokens and any session cookies.

2) role_matrix_20261004.xlsx (attached) — sheet1: role -> permission list; sheet2: examples mapping to API scopes and console capabilities; sheet3: notes on least-privilege recommendations we apply during onboarding.

3) saml_assertions_202609_log.txt (attached, zipped) — extracted SAML event records for 2026-09-01 through 2026-09-30. Each line includes timestamp, request_id, subject_id, authn_context, status (Success/Failure), and a small redaction flag where we redacted IPs and email addresses when required. We will also attach two representative raw assertions (one success, one failure) in separate files so the parser can inspect assertion attributes.

4) scim_delta_export_202609.zip (attached) — batched SCIM change records (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) with attribute list and timestamp. Also included is a brief mapping doc (scim_attribute_map.txt) explaining how our internal attributes map to standard SCIM attributes.

We have placed all files in a read-only Drive folder for convenience: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-healthbridge-evidence (link limited to invitees).

Note on PII: the exports contain names and emails by design (these are identity artifacts). We have redacted IP addresses and session cookies; indicate if you require unredacted IPs for failed assertion troubleshooting and we can discuss an IP-limited handoff process.

If you need these in an alternate CSV/Excel layout, tell us which columns you require and we can re-run the export.

Deliverables attached: access_snapshot_20261004.csv; role_matrix_20261004.xlsx; saml_assertions_202609_log.txt; scim_delta_export_202609.zip

Marissa Cole
Security & Compliance Lead
Redwood Inference

From: Rachel Peters <rachel.peters@healthbridge.com>

Date: 2026-10-06T11:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: access snapshot + SAML assertion traces for SOC 2 review

Marissa — thank you, this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A couple of follow-ups from the assessor after a brief review: 

- Could you include one additional failed SAML assertion example that contains the complete Response envelope (we understand sensitive fields may need redaction).
- For SCIM: please include a small sample of a delta that shows attribute mapping for an automated provisioning event (e.g., assignment -> role change) — the assessor wants to confirm attribute names used for role assignment.

If you can drop the two small additional files into the same Drive folder by EOD tomorrow that would be perfect. We do not need unredacted emails; please leave IPs redacted.

Appreciate the rapid turnaround. If anything blocks you, ping Ben and he can escalate.

Regards,
Rachel
Security Program Manager
HealthBridge
